metadata.title: Exact g-function flows from the staircase model

extraction_notes.note: Sections are opened by the paper's own \resection/\appsection macros, which latex_facts.py does not recognise (0 sections reported); `section` fields were assigned by source offset from those headings, and the appendix title (which contains \ref's) is given as 'A Proofs of equations'.

The labelled numcases blocks (lng0fodd ... lngb2even, g0bodd/g0beven) are not reported as equation facts, so their \ref's do not resolve; each numcases block was emitted as one claim node and the \ref edges to it were added by hand.
equation or claim: kept as claims nested in ClP7 because their parts are justified at different places (b1/b2 in Section 3, g0 in Section 4).
The boundary-condition dictionary (gident) is stated as found empirically and then explicitly assumed; emitted as a conjectural claim plus a separate assumption node rather than as a conjecture.

Cited facts about the staircase / interpolating TBAs stated in prose; typed theorem with origin external per the rule for cited results stated in full, though the source presents them as known physics results rather than theorems.

Much of Section 3-4 content is carried by commutative-diagram flow skeletons and figures (m=5 grid, flow cubes); the displayed diagrams are kept inside the claim/example statements and the figure-only content is not extracted.
The case (i)-(iii) discussions argue and conclude in running text; each was split into a prose proof (the reasoning) and a claim starting at the 'Thus/Translated ... the flow is' sentence.

The unnumbered display after 'the first three terms of (gmodd) therefore become' (\nonumber inside equation) is not a fact and stays inside PP9; figure captions and the 'This explains why the plots ... stabilise' commentary sentences are not nodes.

nodes.name: Boundary kernel $\phi_b$
nodes.statement:
\phi_b(\theta)
&=&-\frac{i}{2\pi}\frac{d}{d\theta}\ln R(\theta)\nonumber\\[4pt]

\phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\theta_0)+

nodes.statement:
\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}
&=
\frac{1}{2}\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\left(-\phi(\theta)-
{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\delta(\theta)\right)\!L(\theta)}\,, \\
\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}
&=
\frac{1}{2}\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\left(
\phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\theta_0)+

\phi(2\theta-\theta_0) -
\phi(2\theta+\theta_0)
\right)\!L(\theta)}\,, \\

\frac{1}{2}\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\left(\phi(\theta-\theta_{b1})+

\phi(\theta-\theta_{b2})+
\phi(\theta+\theta_{b2})\right)\!L(\theta)}\,.

nodes.statement:
Furthermore, in the
crossover region $\ln(r)\approx -(m{-}3)\theta_0/2$ between the
${\cal M}_m$ and ${\cal M}_{m-1}$ plateaux, 
the staircase pseudoenergy
$\epsilon(\theta)$ tends uniformly on suitably-shifted intervals
to the pseudoenergies $\epsilon_i(\theta)$ which solve 
the system of TBA equations
introduced in \cite{Zamolodchikov:1991vx} to describe the
$\phi_{13}$-induced flow from ${\cal M}_{m}$ to ${\cal M}_{m-1}$, a flow which
had previously been

nodes.section: 2 The staircase model, in the bulk and at the boundary
nodes.statement_short: In each crossover region the staircase pseudoenergy tends to the pseudoenergies of the TBA describing the $\phi_{13}$ flow ${\cal M}_m\to{\cal M}_{m-1}$.

nodes.name: Interpolating theory ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$
nodes.statement:
(This interpolating theory was denoted by ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$
in\cite{Zamolodchikov:1991vx}.)

nodes.name: Staircase flows approach the union of ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$ trajectories
nodes.statement:
The natural interpretation of these results -- also backed by
perturbative studies, in the spirit of \cite{Zamolodchikov:1987ti},
at large $m$ \cite{Lassig:1991ab} -- is that 
there is a one-parameter family of integrable quantum field theories 
with renormalisation group trajectories which, in the limit
$\theta_0\to\infty$, approach the union of the renormalisation
group trajectories of the ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$ theories. From now on we
will assume this to be the case, and use it to deduce equations for
the flow of the $g$-function in these same theories.
nodes.section: 2 The staircase model, in the bulk and at the boundary
nodes.statement_short: Assume a one-parameter family of integrable QFTs whose RG trajectories approach the union of the ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$ trajectories as $\theta_0\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Reflection factor by analytic continuation
nodes.statement:
It is natural to suppose that this can be obtained
through the same analytic continuation of the sinh-Gordon
boundary reflection factor as yielded the bulk S-matrix
(\ref{stairS}).

nodes.name: Staircase boundary reflection factor
nodes.statement:
Further continuing to the staircase values of the coupling, this leads
to the following reflection factor:
\begin{equation}
R(\theta)=\frac
{(\frac{1}{2})(\frac{3}{4}-\frac{i\theta_0}{2\pi})
(\frac{3}{4}+\frac{i\theta_0}{2\pi})}
{(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{E}{2})(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{E}{2})
(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{F}{2})(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{F}{2})} \end{equation}
where $E$ and $F$ are two parameters
whose relationship with the original two parameters of the boundary
sinh-Gordon model will not be relevant below.
nodes.section: 2 The staircase model, in the bulk and at the boundary
nodes.statement_short: Boundary reflection factor $R(\theta)$ of the staircase model, with two boundary parameters $E$ and $F$.

nodes.section: 2 The staircase model, in the bulk and at the boundary
nodes.statement_short: Exact $g$-function: $\ln g=\ln g_0+\ln g_b$, an infinite series of kernel-weighted integrals plus a single integral with the boundary kernel $\phi_b$.

nodes.name: Boundary-parameter independence of $\ln g_{b1}$, $\ln g_{b2}$
nodes.statement:
Notice that $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}$ and $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}$ are independent of the boundary
parameters, and $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}$ only depends on the bulk parameter
$\theta_0$ implicitly, via the function $L(\theta)$.

nodes.name: Plateaux of the staircase $g$-function
nodes.statement:
In the large-$\theta_0$ limit, the full $g$-function 
passes through a series of plateaux as $\ln r$ varies, its value on each
plateau always matching  a (conformal) $g$-function value, or a
product of
such values, for the conformal field theory seen by the bulk theory
at that value of $r$.

nodes.name: Minimal model representations and highest weights
nodes.statement:
The model has central charge
$c_m=1-\frac{6}{m(m{+}1)}$, and the permitted irreducible highest-weight
representations of the Virasoro algebra are labelled by pairs of
integers $a$ and $b$ with $1\le a\le m{-}1$ and $1\le b\le m$ subject
to the identifications $(a,b)\sim (m{-}a,m{+}1{-}b)$. They have
highest weight
\begin{equation}
h_{ab}=\frac{((m{+}1)a-mb)^2-1}{4m(m{+}1)}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: ${\cal M}_m$ has central charge $c_m$; its Virasoro representations are labelled by $(a,b)$ modulo $(a,b)\sim(m-a,m+1-b)$, with weights $h_{ab}$.

nodes.name: Conformal boundary conditions are superpositions of Cardy states
nodes.statement:
The most general conformal boundary
condition is a superposition of `pure' (Cardy) boundary
conditions \cite{Cardy:1989ir}.

nodes.name: Boundary entropy of Cardy boundary conditions
nodes.statement_short: Each Cardy boundary condition $(a,b)$ of ${\cal M}_m$ has a $g$-function given by a product of sines.

nodes.name: Spin-flip symmetry of $g(m,a,b)$
nodes.statement:
Notice that this formula respects the identification $(a,b)\cong
(m{-}a,m{+}1{-}b)$, and has the additional symmetries
$g(m,a,b)=g(m,m{-}a,b)$ and $g(m,a,b)=g(m,a,m{+}1{-}b)$. 
This is the ${\mathbb Z}_2$ `spin flip' symmetry
of minimal model boundary conditions which 
in the case of the Ising model
 maps between spin up and spin down Dirichlet
boundaries.

nodes.name: Additivity of boundary entropy
nodes.statement:
For superpositions of Cardy boundaries, the
boundary entropies simply add.

nodes.name: Plateau structure of $L(\theta)$ near ${\cal M}_m$
nodes.statement:
Suppose
the bulk theory is near to the minimal model ${\cal M}_m$, so that
$\ln(r)$ satisfies 
\begin{equation}
-(m{-}2)\theta_0/2 \ll \ln(r)\ll -(m{-}3)\theta_0/2 \,. \end{equation}
Setting
$\alpha=2\ln(1/r)-(m{-}3)\theta_0$, we have
$0\ll\alpha\ll\theta_0$ and, starting from $\theta\approx \ln(1/r)$, 
$L(\theta)$ exhibits an alternating series
of plateaux of lengths $\alpha$ and $\theta_0-\alpha$, the
$i^{\rm th}$ plateau being centred at $\theta=z_i$, where
\begin{equation}
z_i=(m{-}2{-}i)\theta_0/2\,,\qquad i=1, 2,\dots 2m{-}5\,.
\end{equation}
assumptions: the bulk theory is near to the minimal model ${\cal M}_m$
conclusions:
$L(\theta)$ exhibits an alternating series
of plateaux of lengths $\alpha$ and $\theta_0-\alpha$
nodes.statement_short: Near ${\cal M}_m$, $L(\theta)$ shows alternating plateaux of lengths $\alpha$ and $\theta_0-\alpha$ centred at $z_i=(m-2-i)\theta_0/2$.

nodes.name: Constants $x_a$ and $y_a$
Plateau values of $L(\theta)$
nodes.statement:
Starting from $\theta=+\infty$, $L(\theta)$ is close to 
$0$ until $\theta\approx \ln(1/r)$, and then has 
height $\ln(1+x_2)$ for
$\ln(1/r)-\alpha\ll\theta\ll\ln(1/r)$, 
then $\ln(1+y_2)$ for $\ln(1/r)-\theta_0\ll\theta\ll\ln(1/r)-\alpha$, 
then $\ln(1+x_3)$ for
$\ln(1/r)-\theta_0-\alpha\ll\theta\ll\ln(1/r)-\theta_0$, 
and so on, before returning to $0$ for $\theta\ll-\ln(1/r)$. 
In full, the plateau values of $L(\theta)$ are
\begin{align}
\ln(1{+}x_{a}):&~~~~~~~~~~~
z_{2a-3}-\alpha/2\ll\theta\ll 
z_{2a-3}+\alpha/2\,,\qquad~~~~\, a=2\dots m{-}1\,; \\[4pt]
\ln(1{+}y_{a}):&~~~\,
z_{2a-2}-(\theta_0{-}\alpha)/2\ll\theta\ll 
z_{2a-2}+(\theta_0{-}\alpha)/2\,,~~~\, a=2\dots m{-}2\,, \end{align}
and the complete sequence between $\theta=-\ln(1/r)$ and
$\theta=+\ln(1/r)$ is
\begin{equation}
\{
\,
\ln(1{+}x_{m-1}),\,
\ln(1{+}y_{m-2}),\,
\ln(1{+}x_{m-2})\,,
\ln(1{+}y_{m-3})\, \dots\,
\ln(1{+}y_{2}),\,
\ln(1{+}x_{2})
\,
\}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $L(\theta)$ takes values $\ln(1+x_a)$ on $x$-type intervals and $\ln(1+y_a)$ on $y$-type intervals, in the sequence (Ls).

nodes.name: $x$-type and $y$-type intervals
nodes.statement:
As a shorthand we will refer to the intervals in the set 
(\ref{platx}) as $x$-type, and those in the set (\ref{platy}) as
$y$-type.

nodes.name: Formal extension of the plateau sequence
nodes.statement:
From (\ref{xy}),
$\ln(1{+}x_1)= \ln(1{+}y_1)= 0$, and so
we can formally add these two constants to
the end of the sequence (\ref{Ls})
while remaining consistent with the values taken by 
$L(\theta)$ in the corresponding intervals, and likewise add 
$\ln(1{+}y_{m-1})$ and then $\ln(1{+}x_m)$ to the beginning.

nodes.name: Symmetries of plateau values
nodes.statement:
The symmetries $x_a=x_{m+1-a}$, $y_a=y_{m-a}$ reflect the more general
symmetry $L(\theta)=L(-\theta)$.

nodes.name: Plateau values of $\ln g_0$, $\ln g_{b1}$, $\ln g_{b2}$
nodes.statement_short: Near ${\cal M}_m$, $\ln g_0$, $\ln g_{b1}$, $\ln g_{b2}$ are constant, with explicit values depending on the parity of $m$.

nodes.name: Plateau value of $\ln g_0$
Plateau value of $\ln g_{b1}$
nodes.statement:
\begin{numcases}{\hskip -41pt\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}(r)=-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} L(0)=}
-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1{+}x_{(m+1)/2})=
-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m+1}}\right)
&\mbox{for $m$ odd} \\[10pt]
-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1{+}y_{m/2})=
-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}\right)
&\mbox{for $m$ even} \end{numcases}

nodes.name: Plateau value of $\ln g_{b2}$
Derivation of the plateau values of $\ln g_{b1}$, $\ln g_{b2}$
nodes.statement:
Those for $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}$ and $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}$ follow from the fact that
$\phi(\theta)$ and $\phi_{(x)}(\theta)$ are only significantly
non-zero near to $\theta=0$. This means that the integrals (\ref{lngb1})
and (\ref{lngb2}) only 
receive contributions from the regions $\theta\approx 0$ and
$\theta\approx \theta_0/2$, where $L(\theta)$
is, by (\ref{platx}) and (\ref{platy}), 
approximately constant. Pulling $L(\theta)$ out
of each integral and using
\begin{equation}
\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\,\phi(\theta)}=
-\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\,\phi_{(\frac{1}{2})}(\theta)}=\frac{1}{2}\,,\qquad
\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\,\phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta)}=-\frac{1}{4}
\end{equation}
together with the plateau values given by (\ref{platx}) and
(\ref{platy}) leads to (\ref{lngb1odd}) -- (\ref{lngb2even}).
nodes.statement_short: Kernels are localised near $\theta=0$, where $L$ is on a plateau; pull $L$ out of the integrals and use the kernel integrals.

nodes.name: Partial sum equals $\ln g(m,1,1)$ form
nodes.statement_short: The parity-dependent pieces cancel in $\ln g_0+\ln g_{b1}+\ln g_{b2}$, leaving an $m$-uniform closed form.

nodes.name: Partial sum is the $(1,1)$ boundary entropy
nodes.statement:
This is the logarithm of $g(m,1,1)$ or $g(m,m{-}1,1)$, the boundary 
entropy of the
conformal boundary condition associated with the bulk vacuum field or
its ${\mathbb Z}_2$ spin flip conjugate.

nodes.name: Plateau value of $\ln g_{b3}$
nodes.statement:
The integral (\ref{lngb3}) receives
contributions from 
$\theta\approx\pm\theta_{b1}$ and
$\theta\approx\pm\theta_{b2}$\,; if these regions lie within the
$x$- and $y$-type
intervals (\ref{platx}) and (\ref{platy}) 
then, pulling
$L(\theta)$ outside the integrals and recalling that
$L(\theta)=L(-\theta)$,
\begin{equation}
\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}(r)=
{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\left(L\left(\theta_{b1}\right)+L\left(\theta_{b2}\right)\right) \end{equation}
and the value of $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}(r)$ will not change for small changes in
$r$.
assumptions:
if these regions lie within the
$x$- and $y$-type
intervals (\ref{platx}) and (\ref{platy})

nodes.name: Locations of pure-boundary transitions
nodes.statement:
Conversely, $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}(r)$ will undergo a crossover whenever $r$
is such that 
either $\theta_{b1}$ or $\theta_{b2}$ lies on a boundary between the
intervals (\ref{platx}) and (\ref{platy}).
This means that there
will be boundary transitions associated with the parameter
$\theta_{b1}$ at
\begin{equation}
\ln(r)=-k\theta_0-\theta_{b1}\,,\quad  k=0,1,\dots
\end{equation}
and 
\begin{equation}
\ln(r)=-k\theta_0+\theta_{b1}\,,\quad  k=A,A{+}1,\dots
\end{equation}
where $A=\lceil 2\theta_{b1}/\theta_0\rceil$, the smallest integer
greater than or equal to $2\theta_{b1}/\theta_0$\,. An analogous
formula holds for $\theta_{b2}$.

nodes.name: Decoupling of large boundary parameters
nodes.statement:
If $\ln(1/r)$ is smaller than $\theta_{b1}$, $L(\theta)$ is
effectively zero near to $\theta=\pm\theta_{b1}$ and the term
$\frac{1}{2}L(\theta_{b1})$ ceases to contribute to $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}(r)$.

nodes.name: The $(1,1)$ flow
nodes.statement:
If the limit $\theta_{b1}\to\infty$,
$\theta_{b2}\to\infty$ is taken {\em before}\/ $r$ is varied, we 
see that there is one flow which simply moves
through the $(1,1)$ boundary conditions in the successive minimal
models, its $g$-function being given by
$\ln g(r)=\ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}(r)+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}(r)+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}(r)$ for {\em all}\/ values of $r$.

nodes.name: Off-critical lower bound on boundary entropy
nodes.statement:
Notice that since $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}(r)$ is manifestly positive,
all other $g$-function flows must lie above this limiting curve, an
off-critical generalisation of the fact that at a fixed point the
lowest-possible boundary entropy is always found for the $(1,1)$
boundary condition.
assumptions: since $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}(r)$ is manifestly positive
conclusions: all other $g$-function flows must lie above this limiting curve

nodes.name: Possible plateau values seen by boundary parameters
Reduced index ranges
Dictionary between plateau pairs and Cardy superpositions
nodes.statement:
A given pair of boundary parameters corresponds to two (possibly
equal) values of $L(\theta)$ from the set (\ref{lxy}), and, 
via the exponential of
(\ref{lngb3f}) and (\ref{lng0sum}), to a value for the
$g$-function. We found that this value can always be expressed as a
sum of Cardy $g$-function values (\ref{gmab}), according to the
following rules, where we introduce the convenient notation
$[x_a,y_b]$ and so on to denote the particular combinations of boundary
conditions which arise: 
\begin{equation}
\!\!\!
\begin{array}{lll}
 L(\theta_{b1})&L(\theta_{b2})&\mbox{Boundary condition}\\[3pt]
\ln\left(1{+}x_a\right)&\ln\left(1{+}y_b\right)&
\rlap{$[x_a,y_b]$}\phantom{[x_p,x_q]}
\equiv
(b,a)\\
\ln\left(1{+}x_p\right)&\ln\left(1{+}x_q\right)&
[x_p,x_q]\equiv
(1,|p{-}q|{+}1)\&
(1,|p{-}q|{+}3)\&
\cdots\&
(1,m{-}|p{+}q{-}m{-}1|)\\
\ln\left(1{+}y_r\right)&\ln\left(1{+}y_s\right)& 
\rlap{$[y_r,y_s]$}\phantom{[x_p,x_q]}
\equiv
(|r{-}s|{+}1,1)\&
(|r{-}s|{+}3,1)\&
\cdots\&
(m{-}1{-}|r{+}s{-}m|,1)\\
\end{array} \end{equation}
with the same result for $\theta_{b1}\leftrightarrow\theta_{b2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Each pair of plateau values $(L(\theta_{b1}),L(\theta_{b2}))$ gives a $g$-value equal to a sum of Cardy $g$-values, by explicit rules $[x_a,y_b]$, $[x_p,x_q]$, $[y_r,y_s]$.

nodes.name: Dictionary on reduced ranges
nodes.statement:
Notice that if
all indices are restricted to the reduced ranges
(\ref{abr}), the rules simplify to
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{lll}
 L(\theta_{b1})&L(\theta_{b2})&\mbox{Boundary condition}\\[3pt]
\ln\left(1+x_a\right)&\ln\left(1+y_b\right)&(b,a)\\
\ln\left(1+x_p\right)&\ln\left(1+x_q\right)&
(1,|p{-}q|{+}1)\&
(1,|p{-}q|{+}3)\&
\cdots\&
(1,p{+}q{-}1)\\
\ln\left(1+y_r\right)&\ln\left(1+y_s\right)& 
(|r{-}s|{+}1,1)\&
(|r{-}s|{+}3,1)\&
\cdots\&
(r{+}s{-}1,1)\,.
\end{array} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Spin-flip ambiguity of the dictionary
nodes.statement:
The identifications of $g$-function values with specific boundary
conditions implied by (\ref{gident}) should be treated with care for a
couple of reasons. First, ambiguity arises from the equalities
$g(m,a,b)=g(m,m{-}a,b)$, $g(m,a,b)=g(m,a,m{+}1{-}b)$.
These are related to the symmetries 
$L(\theta)=L(-\theta)$, $x_a=x_{m+1-a}$, $y_a=y_{m-a}$
of $L(\theta)$ and its plateau values, and, more precisely, to
the following symmetries of the boundary condition combinations 
given in (\ref{gident}):
\begin{align}
[x_a,y_b]&= [x_{m+1-a},y_{m-b}] &
\overline{[x_a,y_b]}&=
[x_{m+1-a},y_{b}]= [x_{a},y_{m-b}] \nonumber\\[3pt]
[x_p,x_q]&= [x_{m+1-p},x_{m+1-q}]&
\overline{[x_p,x_q]}&=
[x_{m+1-p},x_{q}]= [x_{p},x_{m+1-q}] \\[3pt]
[y_r,y_s]&= [y_{m-r},y_{m-s}]&
\overline{[y_r,y_s]}&=
[y_{m-r},y_{s}]= [y_{r},y_{m-s}] \nonumber
\end{align}
where the overbar denotes the ${\mathbb Z}_2$ `spin flip' symmetry
mentioned just after (\ref{gmab}), acting on individual Cardy
boundaries as $\overline{(a,b)}=(m{-}a,b)\equiv (a,m{+}1{-}b)$\,. 
As remarked in~\cite{Dorey:2009vg}, it should be possible 
to resolve such ambiguities in a systematic fashion
by studying the renormalisation group flows
of the inner products of finite-volume 
excited states~\cite{Bazhanov:1996aq,Dorey:1996re}
with the
boundary states, but we shall leave this for future work.
nodes.statement_short: The dictionary is ambiguous up to the ${\mathbb Z}_2$ spin flip, reflecting symmetries of $L$ and of the bracket combinations.

nodes.name: Accidental degeneracies of $g$-values
nodes.statement:
Second, there are sometimes further, more accidental,
degeneracies in the set of non-negative-integer sums of 
Cardy $g$-function values -- for example,
$g(5,1,3)=2g(5,1,1)$, so that in ${\cal M}_5$ the $(1,3)$ and
$(1,1)\&(1,1)$ boundary conditions cannot be distinguished by their
$g$-function values alone.

nodes.name: Correctness of the dictionary (gident)
nodes.statement:
Nevertheless, and modulo the spin flip
ambiguity just described, (\ref{gident}) is the only set 
of decompositions we have found which works in a uniform fashion for all
$m$. From now on we shall assume that it is correct, and mostly leave
the spin flip ambiguity implicit.

nodes.name: Pure-boundary transitions from $x$- to $y$-type intervals
nodes.statement:
Continuing to suppose that the bulk theory is in 
the vicinity of the bulk fixed point ${\cal M}_m$, we now
let $\ln(r)$ vary from the lower to the upper end of
the range (\ref{rrange}), that is from 
$-(m{-}2)\theta_0/2$ to $-(m{-}3)\theta_0/2$\,. 
The centres of the intervals (\ref{platx}) and (\ref{platy}) 
remain fixed, at $\theta=z_i$, $i=1\dots 2m{-}5$,
but the widths of the $x$-type intervals,
$\alpha\equiv 2\ln(1/r)-(m{-}3)\theta_0$,
decrease from $\theta_0$ to zero, while those of the $y$-type intervals,
$\theta_0-\alpha$, increase from zero to $\theta_0$. Thus so long as
$|\theta_{b1}|< (m{-}2)\theta_0/2$ and $\theta_{b1}$ 
is not an integer multiple of $\theta_0/2$, the regions
$\theta\approx\pm\theta_{b1}$ 
move from $x$-type intervals to $y$-type
intervals during this process, and the value of $L(\pm\theta_{b1})$, and hence
that of the $g$-function, undergoes a change.

nodes.name: Target $y$-plateau of a pure-boundary transition
nodes.statement:
Suppose, then, that at the start of the process $\theta_{b1}$ is
in the $x$-type interval centred at
$\theta=z_{2r-3}$, and $\theta_{b2}$ is in the $x$-type interval centred
at $\theta=z_{2s-3}$, corresponding to plateau values for
$L(\theta_{b1})$ and $L(\theta_{b2})$
equal to $\ln(1+x_r)$ and $\ln(1+x_s)$ respectively.
The $y$-type interval
that $\theta_{b1}$ moves to depends on its position relative to $z_{2r-3}$.
If $\theta_{b1}>z_{2r-3}$ then 
$L(\theta_{b1})$ moves to the plateau $\ln(1+y_{r-1})$, while if
$\theta_{b1}<z_{2r-3}$ it moves to the plateau $\ln(1+y_r)$.

nodes.name: Skeleton of pure-boundary transitions
nodes.statement:
Putting these
ingredients together gives the following `skeleton' of transitions 
from an initial situation where
$L(\theta_{b1})=\ln(1{+}x_r)$ and $L(\theta_{b2})=\ln(1{+}x_s)$\,:
\[
\begin{CD}
[y_{r},y_{s}] @<<< [x_r,y_{s}] @>>> [y_{r-1},y_{s}] \\[2pt]
@AAA @AAA @AAA\\[2pt]
[y_{r},x_{s}] @<<< [x_r,x_{s}] @>>> [y_{r-1},x_{s}] \\[2pt]
@VVV @VVV @VVV\\[2pt]
[y_{r},y_{s-1}] @<<< [x_r,y_{s-1}] @>>> [y_{r-1},y_{s-1}] 
\end{CD}
\]
This diagram encapsulates the boundary flows seen while the bulk is in
the vicinity of ${\cal M}_m$, if $\theta_{b1}$ and $\theta_{b2}$ are in the intervals
$[z_{2r-3}-\theta_0/2,z_{2r-3}+\theta_0/2]$,
$[z_{2s-3}-\theta_0/2,z_{2s-3}+\theta_0/2]$.

nodes.name: Pure-boundary flow grid at $m=5$
nodes.statement:
To give one example, at $m=5$ this
results in a $7\times 7$ grid, the lower ($\theta_{b2}\ge 0$) half of which
is:
\[
\begin{array}{ccccccccccccc}
\vdots &&\vdots &&\vdots &&\vdots &&\vdots &&\vdots &&\vdots \\[2pt]
[y_4,x_3] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_4,x_3] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& 
[y_3,x_3] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_3,x_3] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& 
[y_2,x_3] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_2,x_3] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& 
[y_1,x_3] \\[10pt]
\Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&&
\Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow\\[10pt]
[y_4,y_2] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_4,y_2] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& 
[y_3,y_2] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_3,y_2] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& 
[y_2,y_2] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_2,y_2] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& 
[y_1,y_2] \\[10pt]
\Big\uparrow&& \Big\uparrow&& \Big\uparrow&& \Big\uparrow&&
\Big\uparrow&& \Big\uparrow&& \Big\uparrow\\[10pt]
[y_4,x_2] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_4,x_2] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& 
[y_3,x_2] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_3,x_2] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& 
[y_2,x_2] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_2,x_2] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& 
[y_1,x_2] \\[10pt]
\Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&&
\Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow&& \Big\downarrow\\[10pt]
[y_4,y_1] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_4,y_1] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& 
[y_3,y_1] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_3,y_1] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& 
[y_2,y_1] &\!\!\!\xleftarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& [x_2,y_1] &\!\!\!\xrightarrow{~\quad}\!\!\!& 
[y_1,y_1] 
\end{array}
\]

nodes.name: Symmetries of the pure-boundary flow diagram
nodes.statement:
Notice
that the figure is symmetrical about the diagonals $\theta_{b1}=\theta_{b2}$
and $\theta_{b1}=-\theta_{b2}$, while negating either $\theta_{b1}$ or $\theta_{b2}$ individually
has the same effect as the ${\mathbb Z}_2$ spin flip.
This second feature means that the boundary conditions in the middle
column on the figure, $\theta_{b1}=0$ (or 
equivalently, the top row shown, $\theta_{b2}=0$) are mapped 
into themselves under the
spin flip.
As follows from (\ref{spinflip}), the corresponding
properties hold for all other values of
$m$, if it is assumed that the rules (\ref{gident}) are correct
in general.

nodes.name: Redesignation of plateaux across a bulk transition
nodes.statement:
As this
happens the form of $L(\theta)$ changes: the $x$-type plateaux for
${\cal M}_m$ shrink to zero size, while the $y$-type plateau of
height $\ln(1+y_a)|_{{\cal M}_m}$, $a=1\dots m{-}1$, for ${\cal M}_m$
becomes the $x$-type plateau $\ln(1+x_a)|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$
for ${\cal M}_{m-1}$, with $y$-type plateaux for ${\cal M}_{m-1}$
opening up between these as $\ln(r)$ increases further.
(By (\ref{xy}), $\ln(1+y_a)|_{{\cal M}_m}=\ln(1+x_a)|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$, so 
there is no sudden change in heights implied by the
redesignation of $y$-type to $x$-type plateaux over the transition.)

nodes.name: Bulk-transition change of the partial sum
nodes.statement:
From 
(\ref{lng0sum}), the sum of the first three terms,
$\ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}$, changes from $\ln g(m,1,1)$ to $\ln
g(m{-}1,1,1)$.

nodes.name: Argument for case (i)
nodes.statement:
\noindent {\bf (i)}
If neither $\theta_{b1}$ nor $\theta_{b2}$ are at the centre of
what had been an $x$-type plateau for ${\cal M}_m$, that is if
\begin{equation}
\theta_{b1}, \theta_{b2} \neq (m{-}3)\theta_0/2-k\theta_0\,,\qquad k=0,1,\dots m-3
\end{equation}
then both $\theta_{b1}$ and $\theta_{b2}$ will have undergone a
`pure-boundary' transition of the sort described earlier, from an
$x$-type onto a $y$-type plateau,
{\em before}\/ the ${\cal M}_m\to{\cal M}_{m-1}$ transition is
reached. Thus the conformal boundary condition seen just before
the bulk transition occurs will correspond to some pair
$[y_r,y_s]|_{{\cal M}_m}$ where $2\le r,s\le m{-}2$, corresponding to
$\theta_{b1}$ and $\theta_{b2}$ lying in the intervals
$((m{-}3)\theta_0/2{-}(r{-}1)\theta_0\,,\,(m{-}3)\theta_0/2{-}(r{-}2)\theta_0)$ and
$((m{-}3)\theta_0/2{-}(s{-}1)\theta_0\,,\,(m{-}3)\theta_0/2{-}(s{-}2)\theta_0)$\,.
After the transition the plateau values will
not have changed but their interpretations will have, to the pair
$[x_r,x_s]|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$\,.
nodes.statement_short: Generic boundary parameters have already moved to $y$-type plateaux before the bulk transition, which then relabels them as $x$-type at $m-1$.

nodes.name: Case (i): generic bulk-induced boundary flows
nodes.statement_short: Generic flows take $(f,1)\&\cdots\&(g,1)$ in ${\cal M}_m$ to $(1,f)\&\cdots\&(1,g)$ in ${\cal M}_{m-1}$.

nodes.name: Case (i) fundamental domain
nodes.statement:
Via (\ref{spinflip}) and the symmetry under $\theta_{b1}\leftrightarrow\theta_{b2}$ 
the full set of options is explored by restricting $r$ and $s$ to the
fundamental domain $2\le r\le s\le m-2$, $r+s\le m$. In fact,
(\ref{rsrange}) is equivalent to $f$ and $g$ in (\ref{case1})
being restricted by
\begin{equation}
1\le f<g\le m-1\,,\quad f-g\in 2{\mathbb Z}\,.
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Generic flows go from sinks to sources
nodes.statement:
Notice that these, the generic flows, always start at `sinks'
on networks of pure-boundary flows such as figure \ref{m=5}, and end
on `sources' on the corresponding network one minimal model down.

nodes.name: Argument for case (ii)
nodes.statement:
\noindent {\bf (ii)}
If one of $\theta_{b1}$ or $\theta_{b2}$ lies at the centre of an $x$-type plateau
for ${\cal M}_m$, then it remains on that plateau right up to 
the moment of the bulk transition, after which it will instead lie in
the centre of a $y$-type plateau for ${\cal M}_{m-1}$.
If this centre is located at $\theta=(m-3)\theta_0/2-(s{-}2)\theta_0$, 
$2\le s\le m{-}1$, then the corresponding
value of $L(\theta)$ moves from $\ln(1{+}x_s)|_{{\cal M}_m}$ to
$\ln(1{+}y_{s-1})|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$\,. 
The other plateau value simply changes its designation
from $\ln(1{+}y_r)|_{{\cal M}_m}$ to
$\ln(1{+}x_r)|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$\,, as in case~{\bf (i)}.
nodes.statement_short: A parameter at an $x$-plateau centre moves to a $y$-plateau centre at $m-1$; the other plateau is relabelled as in case (i).

nodes.name: Case (ii) boundary flows
Case (iii) boundary flows
Case (iii) flows decrease the number of Cardy states
nodes.statement:
For these (least-generic) cases the flows are always from sources to 
sinks on neighbouring pairs of pure-boundary
networks such as figure \ref{m=5}, and decrease by 
one the number of superposed Cardy states.

nodes.name: Argument for decoupled boundary parameters
nodes.statement:
Then the corresponding
plateau values of $L(\theta)$ simply flow from zero to zero.
If in addition 
neither $\theta_{b1}$ nor $\theta_{b2}$ lie at the centre of an $x$-type plateau,
then it is easily seen that the situation is covered by case 
{\bf (i)} above, if the indices $r$ and $s$ are allowed to
take the additional values of $1$ and $m{-}1$ (recall that
$\ln(1{+}y_1)|_{{\cal M}_m}=\ln(1{+}y_{m-1})|_{{\cal M}_m}=
\ln(1{+}x_1)|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}=\ln(1{+}x_{m-1})|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}=0$).
nodes.statement_short: Decoupled parameters see $L$ flow from zero to zero, which is case (i) with $r,s$ extended to $1$ and $m-1$.

nodes.name: Combined range of case (i) flows
Enlarged range of case (ii) flows
nodes.statement:
Last of all, if, say,
$|\theta_{b2}|>(m{-}3)\theta_0/2$ while $\theta_{b1}$ is at
the centre of an $x$-type plateau, then the flow is
$[y_1,x_s]|_{{\cal M}_m}\to [x_1,y_{s-1}]|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$
or $[y_{m-1},x_s]|_{{\cal M}_m}\to [x_{m-1},y_{s-1}]|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$ with
$2\le s\le m{-}1$, which simply means that the indices in
(\ref{case2}) can be given the enlarged range
\begin{equation}
1\le r\le m{-}1\,,\quad
2\le s\le m{-}1\,.
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Flow for $\theta_{b1}=180$, $\theta_{b2}=50$
nodes.statement:
Consider $\theta_{b1}=180$,
$\theta_{b2}=50$, one of the highlighted flows
in figures \ref{gflows}d and \ref{firstflows}. 
Focussing on the part of the
flow beginning at $\mathcal{M}_8$, the initial $g$-function
value is close to that of the boundary condition $(1,4)$. Since
$\theta_{b1}>\ln(1/r)$ everywhere in this part of the flow, only 
$\theta_{b2}$ has an effect on the subsequent trajectory.
The centre of the $L(\theta)$ plateau associated with the boundary
condition $(1,4)$ at $\mathcal{M}_8$ is at $\theta=30$, and 
since $\theta_{b2}>30$ 
the flow within $\mathcal{M}_8$ is to $(3,1)$. Then as the bulk
theory flows from $\mathcal{M}_8$ to $\mathcal{M}_7$, the boundary
condition flows to $(1,3)$. The centre of the associated $L(\theta)$
plateau is then at $\theta=60$, and since $\theta_{b2}<60$, the flow within
$\mathcal{M}_7$ is then towards $(3,1)$, and so on. Repeating this
exercise for other values of $\theta_{b2}$ leads to the set of flows 
illustrated in figure~\ref{firstflows}, the second highlighted 
flow of which corresponds to $\theta_{b2}=50$.
nodes.statement_short: Traces the boundary flow from $(1,4)$ at ${\cal M}_8$ through alternating pure-boundary and bulk-induced flows.

nodes.name: Stabilisation with increasing $\theta_{b1}$
nodes.statement:
We remarked while discussing
figure \ref{gflows} that the $g$-function plots
stabilise as $\theta_{b1}$ increases. The same feature can be seen on
comparing figure \ref{firstflows} with
the equivalent diagram for $\theta_{b1}=60$, figure \ref{60}.
For ${\cal M}_3$ and ${\cal M}_4$ the
boundary conditions and flows appearing in figure~\ref{60} match
those in figure \ref{firstflows}, but for the higher minimal
models the boundary conditions appearing are different. This
corresponds to how the plots in figures \ref{gflows}b and
\ref{gflows}d coincide for $\ln r>-60$.

nodes.name: ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$ TBA system
nodes.statement:
The 
TBA system proposed in \cite{Zamolodchikov:1991vx} for ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$
involves $m-2$ pseudoenergies $\epsilon_1\dots\epsilon_{m-2}$, coupled
together by the following system of TBA equations:
\begin{align}
\epsilon_1(\theta)&=\frac{1}{2}\hat{r}\,e^\theta
-\int_{{\mathbb R}}\phi(\theta-\theta')L_2(\theta')\,d\theta' \nonumber\\
\epsilon_a(\theta)&=
-\int_{{\mathbb R}}\phi(\theta-\theta')
(L_{a-1}(\theta')+L_{a{+}1}(\theta'))\,d\theta'\qquad a=2\dots m{-}3 \nonumber\\
\epsilon_{m-2}(\theta)&=\frac{1}{2}\hat{r}\,e^{-\theta}
-\int_{{\mathbb R}}\phi(\theta-\theta')L_{m-1}(\theta')\,d\theta' \end{align}
where $L_a(\theta)=\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_a(\theta)})$\,,
$\phi(\theta)=1/(2\pi\cosh(\theta))$ is as in (\ref{phidef}), and
$\hat{r}$ sets the crossover scale.
nodes.statement_short: Massless TBA for ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$: $m-2$ pseudoenergies coupled along an $A_{m-2}$ chain with left/right-moving driving terms at the ends.

nodes.name: ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$ central charge flow
nodes.statement:
The effective central charge
is then
\begin{equation}
c_{\rm eff}(\hat{r})=\frac{3\hat{r}}{2\pi^2}\int_{{\mathbb R}}
(e^{\theta}L_1(\theta)+
e^{-\theta}L_{m-2}(\theta))\,d\theta
\end{equation}
and as $\ln(\hat{r})$ increases through a region of size of order 1
about the origin, $c_{\rm eff}(\hat{r})$ moves from $c_m$ to
$c_{m-1}$, consistent with the corresponding bulk flow being from ${\cal M}_m$ 
to ${\cal M}_{m-1}$.

nodes.name: Double-scaling limit of the staircase TBA
nodes.statement:
These same equations emerge from a double-scaling limit of
the staircase model if we set
\begin{equation}
\ln(r) = -(m{-}3)\theta_0/2 + \ln(\hat{r})
\end{equation}
and then take the limit $\theta_0\to\infty$ keeping $\ln(\hat{r})$ 
finite, before finally allowing $\ln(\hat{r})$ to vary from
$-\infty$ to $+\infty$. In particular, the pseudoenergies
$\epsilon_a(\theta)$ are recovered from the staircase pseudoenergy
$\epsilon(\theta)$ in the $\theta_0\to\infty$ limit by setting
\begin{equation}
\epsilon_a(\theta)= \epsilon(\theta+(m{-}1{-}2a)\theta_0/2)\,,\qquad
a=1\dots m{-}2 \end{equation}
and only allowing $\theta$ to vary over the full real line
after the limit has been taken.
nodes.statement_short: Setting $\ln r=-(m-3)\theta_0/2+\ln\hat r$ and $\epsilon_a(\theta)=\epsilon(\theta+(m-1-2a)\theta_0/2)$, the staircase TBA tends to the ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$ TBA.

nodes.name: Localisation of the series for $\ln g_0$
nodes.statement:
More precisely, since
$\phi_S(\theta)=\phi(\theta{-}\theta_0)+\phi(\theta{+}\theta_0)$, each term
$\phi_S(\theta_1+\theta_2)\phi_S(\theta_2-\theta_3)\cdots
\phi_S(\theta_n-\theta_1)$
in the sum in (\ref{lng0}) can be expanded as sum of $2^n$
terms of the form
\begin{equation}
\phi(\theta_1+\theta_2-\alpha_1\theta_0)\phi(\theta_2-\theta_3-\alpha_2\theta_0)\cdots
\phi(\theta_n-\theta_1-\alpha_n\theta_0)
\end{equation}
where each $\alpha_k=\pm1$. The decay properties of $\phi(\theta)$ mean that
it is only non-zero for $\theta\approx0$, so for the above term to be
non-zero as $\theta_0\to\infty$ we require
\begin{align}
 \theta_1+\theta_2&\approx\alpha_1\theta_0\nonumber\\
\theta_2-\theta_3&\approx\alpha_2\theta_0\nonumber\\[2pt]
\vdots&\nonumber\\[4pt]
\theta_n-\theta_1&\approx\alpha_n\theta_0
\end{align}
from which it follows that $\theta_k\approx\overline\theta_k$, $k=1\dots n$,
where
\begin{equation}
 \left(\begin{array}{c}
\overline\theta_2\\
\overline\theta_3\\\cdot\\\cdot\\\overline\theta_n\\\overline\theta_1
 \end{array}\right)
=
{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\theta_0\left(\begin{array}{cccccc}
1&1&1&1&\cdots&1\\
1&-1&1&1&\cdots&1\\
1&-1&-1&1&\cdots&1\\
\cdot&\cdot&\cdot&\cdot&&\cdot\\
\cdot&\cdot&\cdot&\cdot&&\cdot\\
1&-1&-1&-1&\cdots&-1
\end{array}\right)
\left(\begin{array}{c}
\alpha_1\\
\alpha_2\\
\cdot\\
\cdot\\
\cdot\\
\alpha_n
\end{array}
\right). \end{equation}
and the integral over ${\mathbb R}^n$ has indeed localised, to a set of $2^n$
regions of size of order one as $\theta_0\to\infty$, which become
infinitely separated in this limit.
The coordinates $\overline\theta_k$ of the
centres of these regions are either all even multiples
of $\theta_0/2$, or all odd multiples of $\theta_0/2$, depending on whether $n$
is even or odd.

For each region of integration we must consider the behaviours
of the `measure factors' $1/(1+e^{\epsilon(\theta_k)})$, $k=1\dots n$.
As for the function $L(\theta)$ discussed above, these factors exhibit
a series of plateaux interleaved by transition regions, at
$\theta\approx\theta_a\equiv (m{-}1{-}2a)\theta_0/2$, 
$a=1\dots m{-}2$. Within these
transition regions, the measure factors
are well-approximated in the $\theta_0\to\infty$ limit by the
functions $1/(1+e^{\epsilon_a})$, by (\ref{epsadef}). In between these
regions the measure factors are approximately constant, and can be
expressed in terms of the numbers $y_a|_{{\cal M}_m}=x_a|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$,
$a=1\dots m{-}1$. Taking these considerations into account,
the terms in the sum in (\ref{lng0}) fall into two categories:
nodes.statement_short: Expand each $\phi_S$ into two shifted bumps; the multiple integrals localise onto $2^n$ separated regions. Measure factors there are either plateau constants or limiting pseudoenergies, splitting terms by the parity of $m+n$.

nodes.name: Non-constant part $\ln g_A$
nodes.statement:
If $m+n$ is odd, every $\overline\theta_k$ satisfying 
$|\overline\theta_k|\le
(m{-}3)\theta/2$ lies in a transition region for $\epsilon(\theta)$, so that
its measure factor remains nontrivial even after the
$\theta_0\to\infty$ limit has been taken.  We denote the
part of $\ln g_0$ consisting of these these terms by $\ln
 g^{\phantom o}_{A}(\hat{r})$.

nodes.name: Constant part $\ln g_B$
nodes.statement:
If $m+n$ is even, every $\overline\theta_k$ lies inside a
plateau of $\epsilon(\theta)$ after the $\theta_0\to\infty$ limit has been
taken, so that the corresponding measure factor becomes constant. We 
denote the ($\hat{r}$-independent) part of $\ln g_0$ consisting 
of these these terms by $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}$.

nodes.name: Anti-trace formula for $\ln g_A$
nodes.statement:
Rewriting the formulae in each subregion of integration in terms of
the limiting pseudoenergies $\epsilon_a(\theta)$ using (\ref{epsadef}) and
shifting the integration variables to remove
all appearances of $\theta_0$, we found that
$\ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}$ can be rewritten in the $\theta_0\to\infty$,
$\hat{r}$ finite limit as
\begin{equation}
\!\ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(\hat{r})\,= 
\!\!\!\sum_{n\ge 1\atop m+n~{\rm odd}}\!\!
\frac{1}{2n}\int_{{\mathbb R}^n}\!\!\mbox{antiTr}
\bigl(\Pi_{i=1}^nA(\theta_i) d\theta_i\bigr)
\phi(\theta_1{-}\theta_2)\phi(\theta_2{-}\theta_3)\cdots
\phi(\theta_{n-1}{-}\theta_n)\phi(\theta_n{+}\theta_1) \end{equation}
where the $(m-2)\times(m-2)$ matrix $A(\theta)$ is given by
\begin{equation}
A(\theta)=
\left(
\begin{array}{cccccccc}
0&\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon_1(\theta)}}&0&0&\cdots&0&0&0\\
\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon_2(\theta)}}&0&
\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon_2(\theta)}}&0&\cdots&0&0&0\\
0&\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon_3(\theta)}}&0&
\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon_3(\theta)}}&\cdots&0&0&0\\[7pt]
\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots\\[7pt]
0&0&0&0&\cdots&
\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon_{m-3}(\theta)}}&0&
\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon_{m-3}(\theta)}}\\
0&0&0&0&\cdots&0&\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon_{m-2}(\theta)}}&0
\end{array}\right) \end{equation}
and $\mbox{antiTr}\bigl(K\bigr)$,
the anti-trace of an $M\times M$ matrix $K$, is defined as 
the sum of its anti-diagonal elements, or equivalently
\begin{equation}
\mbox{antiTr}\bigl(K\bigr)=\mbox{Tr}(KJ)~,
\quad \mbox{where}~ J_{ij}=\delta_{i,M+1-j}\,.
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: In the double-scaling limit $\ln g_A$ is a series of anti-traces of products of the matrix $A(\theta)$ built from the ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$ pseudoenergies.

nodes.name: Constant measure factors for $\ln g_B$
nodes.statement:
The measure factors for the (b) terms are by contrast
constant throughout the relevant integration subregions. They
can therefore be pulled outside their
integrals, leaving only the various factors of
$\phi(\theta)$.
nodes.statement_short: Measure factors are constant on the relevant subregions, so they factor out of the integrals.

nodes.name: Anti-trace series for $\ln g_B$
nodes.statement:
This leads to the following expression for 
$\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}$\,:
\begin{align}
\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}\,&=
\!\!\!\sum_{n\ge 1\atop m+n~{\rm even}}
\frac{1}{2n}\mbox{antiTr}\bigl(B^n\bigr)\!
\int_{{\mathbb R}^n}\!\!\phi(\theta_1{-}\theta_2)\phi(\theta_2{-}\theta_3)
\cdots\phi(\theta_{n-1}{-}\theta_n)\phi(\theta_n{+}\theta_1)
\,d\theta_1\!\cdots d\theta_n\nonumber \\
&=\!\!\!
\sum_{n\ge 1\atop m+n~{\rm even}}
\frac{1}{n2^{n+2}}\,\mbox{antiTr}\left(B^n\right)
\,\,=\!\!
\sum_{n\ge 1\atop m+n~{\rm even}}
\frac{1}{n2^{n+2}}\,\mbox{Tr}\left(B^nJ\right) \end{align}
where the tridiagonal
$(m-3)\times(m-3)$ matrix $B$ is equal to the limit as $\theta_0\to\infty$ of
\[\left(\begin{array}{cccccccc}
0&\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon\left(\frac{m-4}{2}\theta_0\right)}}&0&\cdots&0&0&0\\
\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon\left(\frac{m-6}{2}\theta_0\right)}}&0&
\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon\left(\frac{m-6}{2}\theta_0\right)}}&\cdots&0&0&0\\
0&\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon\left(\frac{m-8}{2}\theta_0\right)}}&0&
\cdots&0&0&0\\[7pt]
\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots\\[7pt]
0&0&0&\cdots&\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon\left(-\frac{m-6}{2}\theta_0\right)}}&0
&\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon\left(-\frac{m-6}{2}\theta_0\right)}}\\
0&0&0&\cdots&0&\frac{1}{1+e^{\epsilon\left(-\frac{m-4}{2}\theta_0\right)}}&0
\end{array}\right)
\]
nodes.statement_short: $\ln g_B=\sum_{m+n\,{\rm even}} \mathrm{Tr}(B^nJ)/(n2^{n+2})$ with $B$ a tridiagonal limit matrix of measure factors.

nodes.name: Explicit form of $B$
nodes.statement:
The explicit form of this matrix can be found using the $L(\theta)$ plateau 
values (\ref{Ls}) and is
\[
\left(\begin{array}{ccccccc}
0&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{m}}&0&\cdots&0&0&0\\
1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{3\pi}{m}}&0&
1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{3\pi}{m}}&\cdots&0&0&0\\
0&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{4\pi}{m}}&0&
\cdots&0&0&0\\[7pt]
\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots\\[7pt]
0&0&0&\cdots&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{(m-3)\pi}{m}}
&0&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{(m-3)\pi}{m}}\\
0&0&0&\cdots&0&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{(m-2)\pi}{m}}&0
\end{array}\right)
\]
or, more concisely,
\begin{equation}
B_{ab}=l_{ab}\,x_{a+1}/(1{+}x_{a+1}) 
\end{equation}
where 
$x_a=x_a|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}=\frac{\sin^2(\pi a/m)}{\sin^2(\pi/m)}-1$\,,
and
$l_{ab}$ is the incidence matrix of the $A_{m-3}$ Dynkin diagram.

nodes.name: Eigenvalues of $B$
nodes.statement:
Note that $B$ is the transpose of a matrix which arises in the
analysis of small fluctuations about stationary solutions of an
associated Y-system \cite{Zamolodchikov:1991vx} and has 
eigenvalues
\begin{equation}
\lambda_k=2\cos\bigl(\frac{\pi k}{m}\bigr)\,,\qquad k=2,3\dots m{-}2\,.
\end{equation}

nodes.name: $B$ commutes with $J$; eigenvector parity
Closed form of $\ln g_B$
nodes.statement:
As explained in appendix A, this information is enough to evaluate
(\ref{g0b}) in closed form, with the result
\begin{numcases}{\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_m} = }
\displaystyle
 ~\ln \left(\left(\frac{4}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!
\frac{\sin\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}}
{\sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}}}\right)
&\mbox{~~for $m$ odd} \\[15pt]
 ~\ln \left(\left(\frac{2}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!\!
\frac{1}{\sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}}}\right)
&\mbox{~~for $m$ even} .
\end{numcases}
nodes.statement_short: $\ln g_B$ for ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$ evaluates in closed form to a log of sines, with different expressions for $m$ odd and even.

nodes.name: Derivation of the plateau value of $\ln g_0$
nodes.statement:
A missing piece of the staircase discussion from the previous section
can now be filled in,
namely the formulae 
(\ref{lng0fodd}) and (\ref{lng0feven})
for the value of $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}|_{{\cal M}_m}$ when the bulk 
staircase theory is in
the vicinity of ${\cal M}_m$. In terms of the limiting $g$-function
equations for ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$, this number is equal to the UV limit of
$\ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(\hat{r}) + \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}$ as $\hat{r}\to 0$.
Considering the limiting forms of the matrix $A(\theta)$, given by
(\ref{Ai}), as $\hat r\to 0$, it is
straightforwardly seen that
\begin{equation}
\ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(0)|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_m}=\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m+1}} \end{equation}
and so
\begin{equation}
\ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}|_{{\cal M}_m} = 
\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m+1}} +
\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_m} 
\end{equation}
\nobreak
which, via (\ref{g0bodd}) and (\ref{g0beven}),
leads immediately to (\ref{lng0fodd}) and
(\ref{lng0feven}).
nodes.statement_short: Identify $\ln g_0$ on ${\cal M}_m$ with the UV limit of $\ln g_A+\ln g_B$; the UV limit of $\ln g_A$ is $\ln g_B$ at $m+1$.

nodes.name: Limiting form of $\ln g_{b1}$
nodes.statement:
When $m$ is odd this remains nontrivial as the 
double-scaling limit is taken and, using
the pseudoenergies defined in (\ref{epsadef}), $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}$ becomes
\begin{equation}
\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}
= -{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\left(\phi(\theta)+
{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\delta(\theta)\right)\!\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{\frac{m-1}{2}}(\theta)})}\,,
\end{equation}
which has UV and IR limits given by (\ref{lngb1odd}) at ${\cal M}_m$ and
(\ref{lngb1even}) at ${\cal M}_{m-1}$ respectively.  When $m$ is even, the 
staircase pseudoenergy instead becomes constant near to
$\theta=0$, giving
\begin{equation}
\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}=-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1+y_{m/2}|^{\phantom o}_{{\cal M}_{m}})
\end{equation}
matching (\ref{lngb1even}) at ${\cal M}_m$ and also (\ref{lngb1odd}) at
${\cal M}_{m-1}$.

nodes.name: Limiting form of $\ln g_{b2}$
nodes.statement:
For $m$ odd, the limiting 
form of $L(\theta\approx\pm\theta_0/2)$ is constant, and
\begin{equation}
\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}=-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln(1+y_{\frac{m-1}{2}}|_{{\cal M}_{m}})
\end{equation}
as in (\ref{lngb2odd}) at ${\cal M}_m$ and (\ref{lngb2even}) at ${\cal M}_{m-1}$.
When $m$ is even, $L(\theta\approx\pm\theta_0/2)$ 
remains nontrivial and in the limit
\begin{equation}
\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}=\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\bigl(\phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta) -
\phi(2\theta)\bigr)\!\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{\frac{m-2}{2}}(\theta)})}\,,
\end{equation}
with UV and IR limits given by (\ref{lngb2even}) at ${\cal M}_m$
and (\ref{lngb2odd}) at ${\cal M}_{m-1}$ respectively.

nodes.name: Rescaled boundary parameters $\hat\theta_{b_i}$
nodes.statement:
To allow the last part of $\ln g^{\phantom o}_b$, $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}$, 
to retain a non-trivial $\hat r$-dependence in
the limit, we pick two integers $a_1$ and $a_2$ with 
$0\le a_i\le m{-}1$, 
write the boundary parameters $\theta_{b1}$ and $\theta_{b2}$ 
as
\begin{equation}
\theta_{b_i}={\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}(m{-}1{-}2a_i)\theta_0 +\hat\theta_{b_i}
\end{equation}
for $i=1,2$, and then
take the $\theta_0\to\infty$ limit
keeping $\hat\theta_{b1}$ 
and $\hat\theta_{b2}$ finite.

nodes.name: Limiting form of $\ln g_{b3}$
nodes.statement:
Given the specification (\ref{epsadef}) of the effective
pseudoenergies $\epsilon_a(\theta)$, 
for $1\le a_i\le m{-}2$
the staircase expression
(\ref{lngb3}) for $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}$ then reduces to
\begin{align}
\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3\,\,a_1a_2}(\hat r,\hat\theta_{b1},\hat\theta_{b2}) &=
{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\sum_{i=1}^2\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\bigl(\phi(\theta-\hat\theta_{b_i})+
\phi(\theta+\hat\theta_{b_i})
\bigr)\!\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{a_i}(\theta)})} \nonumber\\
&=
\sum_{i=1}^2\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\,\phi(\theta-\hat\theta_{b_i})
\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{a_i}(\theta)})} \end{align}
where the symmetry $\epsilon_a(\theta)=\epsilon_{m-1-a}(-\theta)$ 
of the ground-state pseudoenergies for ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$
was used in going from the first line to the second.

nodes.name: Vanishing of decoupled $\ln g_{b3}$ terms
nodes.statement:
If either $a_i$ is equal to $0$ or $m{-}1$, then the
staircase pseudoenergy diverges in the region of $\theta_{b_i}$, and the
corresponding term in (\ref{gbiii}) is zero in the ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$
limit.

nodes.name: Exact $g$-functions for ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$
nodes.statement:
To summarize the results of this section, our final expressions 
for the two-parameter families of exact 
$g$-functions for ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$, indexed by a pair of integers $a_1$
and $a_2$ and expressed in terms of
the rescaled variables $\hat r$, $\hat\theta_{b1}$ and 
$\hat\theta_{b2}$, are as follows:
\vskip -25pt

\begin{align}
\intertext{ $\bullet$ $m$ odd:}
\ln g_{a_1a_2}(\hat{r},\hat\theta_{b1},\hat\theta_{b2}) &=
\ln\!\left(\left(\frac{4}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!\!\!
\sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}}\right)-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\left(\phi(\theta)+
{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\delta(\theta)\right)\!\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{\frac{m-1}{2}}(\theta)})}
\nonumber\\[5pt]
&\quad\qquad +\ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(\hat{r})
+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3\,\,a_1a_2}(\hat r,\hat\theta_{b1},\hat\theta_{b2})\,; \\
\intertext{ $\bullet$ $m$ even:}
\ln g_{a_1a_2}(\hat{r},\hat\theta_{b1},\hat\theta_{b2}) &=
\ln\!\left(\left(\frac{2}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!\!\!
\sqrt{\sin\frac{\pi}{m}}\right)+\int_{{\mathbb R}}{d\theta\Bigl(\phi_{(\frac{3}{4})}(\theta)
- \phi(2\theta)\Bigr)\ln(1+e^{-\epsilon_{\frac{m-2}{2}}(\theta)})}
\nonumber\\[5pt]
&\quad\qquad 
+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(\hat{r})
+\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3\,\,a_1a_2}(\hat
r,\hat\theta_{b1},\hat\theta_{b2})\,. \end{align}

In both cases $g^{\phantom o}_{A}$ is given by (\ref{goA}), the
sum over $n$ running through even integers for $m$ odd, and 
odd integers for $m$ even, with the pseudoenergies involved
solving the bulk
${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$ TBA system (\ref{bulkmasslessTBA}). The term
$g^{\phantom o}_{b3\,\,a_1a_2}$ is as defined in (\ref{gbiii}).
nodes.statement_short: Two-parameter families of exact $g$-function equations for the ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$ flows: a constant plus $\ln g_{b1}$ or $\ln g_{b2}$, $\ln g_A$ and $\ln g_{b3\,a_1a_2}$.

nodes.name: Origin of the constant terms
nodes.statement:
The
constant terms result from adding $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}$, given by
(\ref{g0bodd}) or (\ref{g0beven}), to $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}$ for $m$ odd, and to
$\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}$ for $m$ even. The remaining integral term is $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}$
for $m$ odd and $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}$ for $m$ even.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the closed form of $\ln g_B$ with the constant $\ln g_{b1}$ or $\ln g_{b2}$ limit.

nodes.name: Limiting one- and zero-parameter families
nodes.statement:
Formally setting one or both
of $a_1$ and $a_2$ equal to $0$ or $m{-}1$, as discussed after
(\ref{gbiii}), incorporates the
limiting one- and zero- parameter families
of flows found by deleting the $\hat\theta_{b1}$ and/or
$\hat\theta_{b2}$ dependent parts of $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}$.

nodes.name: Zero-parameter flow from $g(m,1,1)$ to $g(m-1,1,1)$
nodes.statement:
If both are
deleted so that $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b3}$ is identically zero, 
then by the results of the last section the
$g$-function flow should be from $g(m,1,1)$ at $\hat r=0$ to
$g(m{-}1,1,1)$ as $\hat r\to\infty$.

nodes.name: UV and IR checks of the zero-parameter flow
nodes.statement:
This can be checked directly.
Simplest is the UV limit. For $m$ odd, 
using (\ref{lngb1odd})
and (\ref{gUV}),
the first three terms on the RHS of (\ref{gmodd}) tend to
\begin{equation}
\ln\left(\left(\frac{4}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}
\!\!\sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m}}}\right)
-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi}{m+1}\right)}\right)
+\ln\left(\left(\frac{2}{m+1}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}
\frac{1}{\sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m+1}}}}\right)
\end{equation}
which is equal to $g(m,1,1)$\,.
Similarly, for $m$ even, (\ref{lngb2even}) and (\ref{gUV})
imply that the first three terms on the RHS of
(\ref{gmeven}) become
\begin{equation}
\ln\left(\left(\frac{2}{m}\right)^{\!\frac{1}{4}}\!\!
\sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m}}}\right)
-
{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln\left(\frac{\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi m}{2(m+1)}\right)}
{\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi}{m+1}\right)}\right)
+
\ln\left(\left(\frac{4}{m{+}1}\right)^{\!\frac{1}{4}}
\frac{\,\sin\left(\frac{m\pi}{2(m+1)}\right)}
{\sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m+1}}}}\right)
\end{equation}
\nobreak
and the value of $g(m,1,1)$ is again reproduced.
\goodbreak

In the $\hat r\to\infty$, IR, limit
the matrix $A(\theta_i)$ defined in (\ref{Ai}) again becomes independent
of $\theta$ in the central region $\theta\approx 0$ where the integrals in
(\ref{goA}) have their support, and tends to the following 
$(m{-}2)\times (m{-}2)$ matrix:
\begin{equation}
A_{\rm IR}=
\left(\begin{array}{cccccccc}
0&0&0&\cdots&0&0&0\\
1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m-1}}{\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{m-1}}&0
&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m-1}}{\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{m-1}}&\cdots&0&0&0\\
0&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m-1}}{\sin^2\frac{3\pi}{m-1}}
&0&\cdots&0&0&0\\
&&&&&&\\
\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots\\
&&&&&&\\
0&0&0&\cdots&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m-1}}{\sin^2\frac{(m-3)\pi}{m-1}}
&0&1-\frac{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m-1}}{\sin^2\frac{(m-3)\pi}{m-1}}\\
0&0&0&\,\cdots\,&0&~~0~~&0
\end{array}\right).\end{equation}
In terms of $A_{\rm IR}$\,,
\begin{equation}
\ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(\infty)=\sum_{n\ge 1\atop m+n~{\rm odd}}
\frac{1}{n2^{n+2}}\,\mbox{Tr}\left((A_{\rm IR})^nJ\right).
\end{equation}
To evaluate this sum, observe that the central $(m{-}4)\times(m{-}4)$
sub-matrix of $A_{\rm IR}$ is the matrix $B$ for ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}$.
Furthermore, the zero values of all entries in the first and final
rows means that the central $(m{-}4)\times(m{-}4)$ sub-matrix of 
$(A_{\rm IR})^n$ is just 
$(B|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}})^n$\,, 
and the entries on the first and final rows are again zero.
Hence the traces and antitraces of $(A_{\rm IR})^n$ are equal to those
of $(B|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}})^n$\,, and 
\begin{equation}
\ln g_{0_A}(\infty)|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m}}=\ln g_{0_B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}}
\end{equation}
allowing (\ref{g0bodd}) and (\ref{g0beven}) at $m{-}1$
to be used to compute
$\ln g_{0_A}(\infty)|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m}}$\,.
For $m$ odd, using (\ref{lngb1even}) and
(\ref{g0beven}) at $m{-}1$,
the first three terms of (\ref{gmodd}) therefore become
\begin{equation}
\ln\left(\left(\frac{4}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!\!
\sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m}}}\right)
-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi}{m-1}\right)}\right)
+ \ln\left(\left(\frac{2}{m-1}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!\!
\frac{1}{\sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m-1}}}}\right)
\nonumber\\
\end{equation}
which is indeed equal to $g(m{-}1,1,1)$. 
Similarly, for $m$ even, in the $\hat r\to\infty$ limit 
the first three terms of (\ref{gmeven}) are, by 
(\ref{lngb2odd}) and (\ref{g0bodd}) at $m{-}1$,
\begin{equation}
\ln\left(\left(\frac{2}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\!\!
\sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m}}}\right)
-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\ln\left(\frac{\sin^2\left(\frac{(m-2)\pi}{2(m-1)}
\right)}{\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi}{m-1}\right)}\right)
+\ln\left(\left(\frac{4}{m-1}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}
\frac{\sin\left(\frac{(m-2)\pi}{2(m-1)}\right)}
{\sqrt{\sin{\frac{\pi}{m-1}}}}\right)
\end{equation}
which again matches $g(m{-}1,1,1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Direct evaluation of the UV and IR limits of the constant terms for $m$ odd and even. The IR step reduces $A_{\rm IR}$ to the $B$ matrix of ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}$.

nodes.name: Cube of ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$ boundary flows
nodes.statement:
More generally, the full equations (\ref{gmodd}) or (\ref{gmeven})
predict a collection of two-parameter families of
flows, indexed by the two integers $a_1$ and $a_2$.
The relevant calculations have been carried out in the last section
and we won't repeat them here. Instead, in figure \ref{cubef} below we
show a typical family of flows,
where $r=a_1+1$ and $s=a_2+1$. 
All flows for $\hat\theta_{b1}$ and $\hat\theta_{b2}$ finite start in the far UV at
the $[x_r,x_s]$ boundary of ${\cal M}_m$, a superposition of Cardy
boundaries given by the rule (\ref{gident}). If both $\hat\theta_{b1}$ and
$\hat\theta_{b2}$ are zero, the flow is directly downwards to the
$[y_{r-1},y_{s-1}]$ boundary of ${\cal M}_{m-1}$, driven by the bulk
perturbation. Nonzero values of $\hat\theta_{b1}$ and $\hat\theta_{b2}$ 
correspond to the addition of boundary perturbations to the bulk
perturbation, and cause the
trajectory to visit other boundaries on its way from UV to IR, as can
be read from the figure.

nodes.name: Truncation of the cube of flows
nodes.statement:
If either of $a_1$ or $a_2$ is equal to $1$ or $m{-}2$, so that one or
both of $r$ and $s$ is equal to $2$ or $m{-}1$, the cube shown in
figure \ref{cubef} truncates, the equalities $x_1=y_1$ or
$x_{m-1}=y_{m-2}$ within ${\cal M}_{m-1}$ causing one or two rows on the
bottom face of the cube to fuse together, resulting in the
flow patterns illustrated in
figure \ref{cubetrunc}.

nodes.name: Generalise Pozsgay's approach to non-diagonal scattering
nodes.statement:
The formulae found in section~\ref{gMAplus}
describe, for the first time, exact off-critical $g$-functions
in situations where the underlying scattering theory is
non-diagonal, and it will be interesting to generalise the approach of
Pozsgay~\cite{Pozsgay:2010tv} to cover such cases.

nodes.name: Abelianisation of TBA descriptions
nodes.statement:
Finally, it is noteworthy how the embedding of non-diagonal bulk and 
boundary scattering theories within higher-dimensional manifolds of 
integrability achieved by the staircase and HSG models manages to
`abelianise' their TBA descriptions. It would be very interesting to
know how general this phenomenon is, and to understand it at a deeper
level.

nodes.name: Proof of the closed form of $\ln g_B$
nodes.statement:
To derive (\ref{g0bodd}) and (\ref{g0beven}) from (\ref{g0b}), we 
first convert the final sum, over traces of products of powers of $B$
with $J$,
into a sum of traces of pure powers of
related matrices, after which the identity
\begin{equation}
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n}\mbox{Tr}\,M^n
= -\mbox{Tr}\ln(I-M)
= -\ln\mbox{Det}(I-M) \end{equation}
will allow the sum to be evaluated in terms of the eigenvalues of
these related matrices. There are two cases. 

\medskip

\noindent $\bullet$ If $m$ is odd, then the sum 
in (\ref{g0b}) is over odd powers of $B$. Shuffling indices and
using the symmetries of $B$ it can be checked that $B^nJ=(BJ)^n$ for
all odd $n$, and so 
\begin{eqnarray}
 \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}&=&
\frac{1}{4}
\mbox{Tr}
\sum_{n\ge 1\atop n {\rm odd}}
\frac{1}{n}\left({\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)^n\nonumber\\
&=&\frac{1}{8}
\ln\frac{\mbox{Det}\left(1+{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}{\mbox{Det}\left(1-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}
BJ\right)}\,. \end{eqnarray}
From (\ref{Jparity}), the
eigenvalues of $BJ$ are $(-1)^k\lambda_k$, which for $m$ odd are the
numbers $2\cos(2\pi/m)$, $2\cos(4\pi/m)$\,\dots
$2\cos((m{-}3)\pi/m)$, all with multiplicity two. Hence 
\begin{equation}
\frac{\mbox{Det}\left(1+{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}{\mbox{Det}\left(1-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}
BJ\right)}=
\frac{\cos^4\frac{\pi}{m}\cos^4\frac{2\pi}{m}\cdots\cos^4\frac{(m-3)\pi}{2m}}
{\sin^4\frac{\pi}{m}\sin^4\frac{2\pi}{m}\cdots\sin^4\frac{(m-3)\pi}{2m}}\,.
\end{equation}
To evaluate this we call upon some well-known trigonometric
identities. For the numerator we use
\begin{equation}
\cos\frac{\pi}{n}\cos\frac{2\pi}{n}\cdots\cos\frac{(n-1)\pi}{2n}=
\frac{1}{2^{(n-1)/2}}\quad\mbox{for $n$ odd} \end{equation}
and for the denominator 
\begin{equation}
\sin\frac{\pi}{n}\sin\frac{2\pi}{n}\cdots\sin\frac{(n-1)\pi}{n}=
\frac{n}{2^{n-1}} \end{equation}
which implies
\begin{equation}\sin^2\frac{\pi}{n}\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{n}\cdots\sin^2\frac{(n-1)\pi}{2n}
=\frac{n}{2^{n-1}}\quad\mbox{for $n$ odd.} \end{equation}
Using (\ref{trig0}) and (\ref{trig2}),
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\mbox{Det}\left(1+{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}
{\mbox{Det}\left(1-{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} BJ\right)}=
\frac{1}{m^2}\frac{\sin^4\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}}{\cos^4\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}}
=\left(\frac{4}{m}\frac{\sin^4\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}}
{\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}\right)^2
\end{equation}
and so (\ref{lnodd}) is in agreement with (\ref{g0bodd}).

\medskip

\noindent $\bullet$ If $m$ is even, then the sum in (\ref{g0b}) is 
instead over even powers of $B$. This time we make use of the
identity, valid for $m$ even, that
\begin{equation} 
\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)=\mbox{Tr}(B^n-B^{\prime n}) \end{equation}
where $B^{\prime}$ is the $(m-3)\times(m-3)$ matrix which only differs
from $B$ in the following elements:
\begin{equation}
B^{\prime}_{\frac{m-2}{2},\frac{m-4}{2}}=
B^{\prime}_{\frac{m-2}{2},\frac{m}{2}}=0. \end{equation}
To prove this identity we write the LHS as
\begin{equation} 
\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)=
B_{i_1i_2}B_{i_2i_3}\cdots B_{i_{n-1}i_{n}}B_{i_{n}m-i_1-2} \end{equation}
and note the following properties of $B$:
\begin{eqnarray}
B_{i,i-1}&=&B_{i,i+1}, \mbox{\quad all other entries $0$;} \\
B_{ij}&=&B_{m-2-i,m-2-j}\,.  \end{eqnarray}
The first of these means that (\ref{Banti}) can be interpreted as a
weighted sum over all $n$-step paths on the $A_{m-3}$ Dynkin diagram which
start and finish at pairs of conjugate nodes
$i_1$ and
$m{-}2{-}i_1$, $i_1=1\dots m{-}3$,
and move by one link at each step.
Likewise $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ and $\mbox{Tr}(B'^n)$ are 
weighted sums over
$n$-step paths on the same Dynkin diagram, but which this time
start and finish at the same node $i_1$, where again $i_1$ is summed
from $1$ to $m{-}3$.

These observations imply that both sides of (\ref{Banti}) are zero for
$n$ odd, and so from now on we can take $n$ to be even (which is the
case of direct interest in the current context). 
Due again to (\ref{B0}), a term in $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ with
$i_1<\frac{m-2}{2}$ must include the element
$B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$, and a term with
$i_1>\frac{m-2}{2}$ must include the element
$B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m-4}{2}}$. 
Assume first that $i_1<\frac{m-2}{2}$, and consider
\begin{equation}
B_{i_1i_2}B_{i_2i_3}\cdots B_{i_{n-1}i_{n}}B_{i_{n},m-2-i_1} \end{equation}
for some particular $i_2\dots i_n$. Suppose
$B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$ appears for the final time at
$B_{i_pi_{p+1}}$, which means that
$B_{i_{p+1}i_{p+2}}=B_{\frac{m}{2}\frac{m+2}{2}}$. 
By (\ref{B1}), the value of (\ref{Bterm}) is unchanged if all
indices $i_q$ with $q>p$ are replaced by their conjugates
$m-2-i_q$. The resulting term appears in the
trace not of $B^nJ$, but of $B^n$. Similarly, every term in the
expansion of $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ with $i_1>\frac{m-2}{2}$ can be equated
with a term in the expansion of $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ with
$i_1>\frac{m-2}{2}$\,. Finally,
the terms in the expansions of $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ and $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$
with $i_1=\frac{m-2}{2}$ are already equal, since $i_1$ is then equal
to $m-2-i_1$. Thus $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ is equal to the sum of the terms
in the trace of $B^n$ that include either
$B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$ or
$B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m-4}{2}}$ at least once. Now the trace of 
$B'^n$ as defined by (\ref{BPdef})
is equal to the trace of
$B^n$ minus the terms where $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$ or
$B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m-4}{2}}$ appears at least once. Hence
$\mbox{Tr}(B^n-B^{\prime n})$ gives the required terms and
(\ref{traceident}) holds.

If $m$ is even we therefore have
\begin{eqnarray}
 \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}&=&
\sum_{n>1\atop n~{\rm even}}
\frac{1}{n2^{n+2}}\mbox{Tr}\,(B^nJ)\nonumber \\
&=&\frac{1}{4}
\sum_{n>1\atop n~{\rm even}}
\frac{1}{n}\mbox{Tr}\left(\left({\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}
B\right)^n-\left({\textstyle\frac{1}{2}} B^{\prime}\right)^n\right)\nonumber\\
&=&\frac{1}{8}\ln
\frac{\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}(B^{\prime})^2\right)}
{\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}B^2\right)} \end{eqnarray}
using (\ref{lntr}).
To find the eigenvalues of $B'$, $\mbox{Det}(B'-\lambda I)$ can be
expanded
about the middle row to see that the characteristic polynomial of $B'$ 
is proportional to $\lambda$ times the product of the (equal)
characteristic polynomials of the upper-left and lower-right 
$(m{-}4)/2\times (m{-}4)/2$ submatrices of $B'$, which we denote
$B'_1$ and $B'_2$. These submatrices can
be fully diagonalised using the $(m{-}4)/2$ eigenvectors $\psi_k$
of $B$ with $k$ odd: from (\ref{Jparity}), these eigenvectors satisfy
$J\psi_k=-\psi_k$. Hence their middle
components are zero, while the neighbouring two are the
negatives of each other. Given the definition (\ref{BPdef}) of $B'$
this means that projecting each $\psi_k$ for $k$ odd
onto its first $(m{-}4)/2$
components yields $(m{-}4)/2$ independent eigenvectors of $B'_1$
with eigenvalues $\lambda_k$, and likewise for $B'_2$. 
Hence the eigenvalues of $B'$ are
\begin{equation}
\lambda_k=2\cos\bigl(\frac{\pi k}{m}\bigr)\,,\qquad k=3,5\dots m{-}3\,, \end{equation}
each with multiplicity $2$, together with $0$.
If $m=2$ mod $4$, then $0$ is also in
the set (\ref{elist}), and so
the algebraic multiplicity of the zero eigenvalue is $3$, even though its 
geometric multiplicity turns out to be only $2$. However, this lack of full 
diagonalisability makes no difference to the computations of traces.

We can now calculate $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}$. Evaluating
(\ref{lneven}) using the eigenvalues just obtained,
\begin{eqnarray}
 \frac{\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}(B^{\prime})^2\right)}
{\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}B^2\right)}&=&
\frac{\sin^4\frac{3\pi}{m}\sin^4\frac{5\pi}{m}\cdots
\sin^4\frac{(m-3)\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{m}\sin^2
\frac{3\pi}{m}\cdots\sin^2\frac{(m-2)\pi}{m}}\nonumber\\
&=&\frac{\sin^2\frac{3\pi}{m}\sin^2\frac{5\pi}{m}\cdots
\sin^2\frac{(m-3)\pi}{m}}{\sin^2\frac{2\pi}{m}\sin^2
\frac{4\pi}{m}\cdots\sin^2\frac{(m-2)\pi}{m}}\,. \end{eqnarray}
Labelling the final numerator $X$ and the denominator $Y$,
(\ref{trig}) at $n=m$ and $n=m/2$ respectively implies that
\begin{equation}
XY=\frac{1}{\sin^4\frac{\pi}{m}}\left(\frac{m}{2^{m-1}}\right)^2~,\qquad
Y=\frac{m^2}{2^{m}}\,.
\end{equation}
Hence
\begin{equation} 
\frac{X}{Y}=\frac{\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}(B^{\prime})^2\right)}
{\mbox{Det}\left(I-\frac{1}{4}B^2\right)}=
\left(\frac{2}{m\sin^2\frac{\pi}{m}}\right)^2
\end{equation}
\nobreak
and (\ref{lneven}) agrees with (\ref{g0beven}).
nodes.statement_short: Convert the anti-trace sums into traces of powers, sum them with $\sum \mathrm{Tr}M^n/n=-\ln\mathrm{Det}(I-M)$, and evaluate via eigenvalues. Odd $m$ uses $B^nJ=(BJ)^n$; even $m$ uses $\mathrm{Tr}(B^nJ)=\mathrm{Tr}(B^n-B'^n)$ and trigonometric product identities.

nodes.name: Trace identity for $m$ even
nodes.statement_short: For $m$ even, $\mathrm{Tr}(B^nJ)=\mathrm{Tr}(B^n-B'^n)$ where $B'$ deletes two middle-row entries of $B$.

nodes.name: Proof of the trace identity
nodes.statement:
To prove this identity we write the LHS as
\begin{equation} 
\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)=
B_{i_1i_2}B_{i_2i_3}\cdots B_{i_{n-1}i_{n}}B_{i_{n}m-i_1-2} \end{equation}
and note the following properties of $B$:
\begin{eqnarray}
B_{i,i-1}&=&B_{i,i+1}, \mbox{\quad all other entries $0$;} \\
B_{ij}&=&B_{m-2-i,m-2-j}\,.  \end{eqnarray}
The first of these means that (\ref{Banti}) can be interpreted as a
weighted sum over all $n$-step paths on the $A_{m-3}$ Dynkin diagram which
start and finish at pairs of conjugate nodes
$i_1$ and
$m{-}2{-}i_1$, $i_1=1\dots m{-}3$,
and move by one link at each step.
Likewise $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ and $\mbox{Tr}(B'^n)$ are 
weighted sums over
$n$-step paths on the same Dynkin diagram, but which this time
start and finish at the same node $i_1$, where again $i_1$ is summed
from $1$ to $m{-}3$.

These observations imply that both sides of (\ref{Banti}) are zero for
$n$ odd, and so from now on we can take $n$ to be even (which is the
case of direct interest in the current context). 
Due again to (\ref{B0}), a term in $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ with
$i_1<\frac{m-2}{2}$ must include the element
$B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$, and a term with
$i_1>\frac{m-2}{2}$ must include the element
$B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m-4}{2}}$. 
Assume first that $i_1<\frac{m-2}{2}$, and consider
\begin{equation}
B_{i_1i_2}B_{i_2i_3}\cdots B_{i_{n-1}i_{n}}B_{i_{n},m-2-i_1} \end{equation}
for some particular $i_2\dots i_n$. Suppose
$B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$ appears for the final time at
$B_{i_pi_{p+1}}$, which means that
$B_{i_{p+1}i_{p+2}}=B_{\frac{m}{2}\frac{m+2}{2}}$. 
By (\ref{B1}), the value of (\ref{Bterm}) is unchanged if all
indices $i_q$ with $q>p$ are replaced by their conjugates
$m-2-i_q$. The resulting term appears in the
trace not of $B^nJ$, but of $B^n$. Similarly, every term in the
expansion of $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ with $i_1>\frac{m-2}{2}$ can be equated
with a term in the expansion of $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$ with
$i_1>\frac{m-2}{2}$\,. Finally,
the terms in the expansions of $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ and $\mbox{Tr}(B^n)$
with $i_1=\frac{m-2}{2}$ are already equal, since $i_1$ is then equal
to $m-2-i_1$. Thus $\mbox{Tr}(B^nJ)$ is equal to the sum of the terms
in the trace of $B^n$ that include either
$B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$ or
$B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m-4}{2}}$ at least once. Now the trace of 
$B'^n$ as defined by (\ref{BPdef})
is equal to the trace of
$B^n$ minus the terms where $B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m}{2}}$ or
$B_{\frac{m-2}{2}\frac{m-4}{2}}$ appears at least once. Hence
$\mbox{Tr}(B^n-B^{\prime n})$ gives the required terms and
(\ref{traceident}) holds.
nodes.statement_short: Interpret traces as weighted path sums on the $A_{m-3}$ Dynkin diagram and reflect path tails through the middle node to match terms.

nodes.name: Kernels localised
nodes.statement:
Those for $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b1}$ and $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{b2}$ follow from the fact that
$\phi(\theta)$ and $\phi_{(x)}(\theta)$ are only significantly
non-zero near to $\theta=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Kernels are localised near the origin

nodes.name: Contributions from plateaux
nodes.statement:
This means that the integrals (\ref{lngb1})
and (\ref{lngb2}) only 
receive contributions from the regions $\theta\approx 0$ and
$\theta\approx \theta_0/2$, where $L(\theta)$
is, by (\ref{platx}) and (\ref{platy}), 
approximately constant.
nodes.statement_short: Integrals only see plateau regions of $L$

nodes.name: Pull out $L$
nodes.statement_short: Factor out $L$ and use the kernel integrals

nodes.name: Generic parameters already moved
nodes.statement:
\noindent {\bf (i)}
If neither $\theta_{b1}$ nor $\theta_{b2}$ are at the centre of
what had been an $x$-type plateau for ${\cal M}_m$, that is if
\begin{equation}
\theta_{b1}, \theta_{b2} \neq (m{-}3)\theta_0/2-k\theta_0\,,\qquad k=0,1,\dots m-3
\end{equation}
then both $\theta_{b1}$ and $\theta_{b2}$ will have undergone a
`pure-boundary' transition of the sort described earlier, from an
$x$-type onto a $y$-type plateau,
{\em before}\/ the ${\cal M}_m\to{\cal M}_{m-1}$ transition is
reached.
nodes.statement_short: Generic parameters transition to $y$-type before the bulk transition

nodes.name: Boundary condition before bulk transition
nodes.statement:
Thus the conformal boundary condition seen just before
the bulk transition occurs will correspond to some pair
$[y_r,y_s]|_{{\cal M}_m}$ where $2\le r,s\le m{-}2$, corresponding to
$\theta_{b1}$ and $\theta_{b2}$ lying in the intervals
$((m{-}3)\theta_0/2{-}(r{-}1)\theta_0\,,\,(m{-}3)\theta_0/2{-}(r{-}2)\theta_0)$ and
$((m{-}3)\theta_0/2{-}(s{-}1)\theta_0\,,\,(m{-}3)\theta_0/2{-}(s{-}2)\theta_0)$\,.
nodes.statement_short: Identify the pair $[y_r,y_s]$ at ${\cal M}_m$

nodes.name: Relabelling after transition
nodes.statement:
After the transition the plateau values will
not have changed but their interpretations will have, to the pair
$[x_r,x_s]|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$\,.
nodes.statement_short: Plateau values reinterpreted as $[x_r,x_s]$ at $m-1$

nodes.name: Parameter stays at plateau centre
nodes.statement:
\noindent {\bf (ii)}
If one of $\theta_{b1}$ or $\theta_{b2}$ lies at the centre of an $x$-type plateau
for ${\cal M}_m$, then it remains on that plateau right up to 
the moment of the bulk transition, after which it will instead lie in
the centre of a $y$-type plateau for ${\cal M}_{m-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: A centred parameter moves to a $y$-plateau centre

nodes.name: Plateau value change
nodes.statement:
If this centre is located at $\theta=(m-3)\theta_0/2-(s{-}2)\theta_0$, 
$2\le s\le m{-}1$, then the corresponding
value of $L(\theta)$ moves from $\ln(1{+}x_s)|_{{\cal M}_m}$ to
$\ln(1{+}y_{s-1})|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$\,.
nodes.statement_short: Value moves from $\ln(1+x_s)$ to $\ln(1+y_{s-1})$

nodes.name: Other plateau relabelled
nodes.statement:
The other plateau value simply changes its designation
from $\ln(1{+}y_r)|_{{\cal M}_m}$ to
$\ln(1{+}x_r)|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$\,, as in case~{\bf (i)}.
nodes.statement_short: Other value relabelled as in case (i)

nodes.name: Expand kernel product
nodes.statement:
More precisely, since
$\phi_S(\theta)=\phi(\theta{-}\theta_0)+\phi(\theta{+}\theta_0)$, each term
$\phi_S(\theta_1+\theta_2)\phi_S(\theta_2-\theta_3)\cdots
\phi_S(\theta_n-\theta_1)$
in the sum in (\ref{lng0}) can be expanded as sum of $2^n$
terms of the form
\begin{equation}
\phi(\theta_1+\theta_2-\alpha_1\theta_0)\phi(\theta_2-\theta_3-\alpha_2\theta_0)\cdots
\phi(\theta_n-\theta_1-\alpha_n\theta_0)
\end{equation}
where each $\alpha_k=\pm1$.
nodes.statement_short: Expand $\phi_S$ products into $2^n$ shifted terms

nodes.name: Localisation of integrals
nodes.statement:
The decay properties of $\phi(\theta)$ mean that
it is only non-zero for $\theta\approx0$, so for the above term to be
non-zero as $\theta_0\to\infty$ we require
\begin{align}
 \theta_1+\theta_2&\approx\alpha_1\theta_0\nonumber\\
\theta_2-\theta_3&\approx\alpha_2\theta_0\nonumber\\[2pt]
\vdots&\nonumber\\[4pt]
\theta_n-\theta_1&\approx\alpha_n\theta_0
\end{align}
from which it follows that $\theta_k\approx\overline\theta_k$, $k=1\dots n$,
where
\begin{equation}
 \left(\begin{array}{c}
\overline\theta_2\\
\overline\theta_3\\\cdot\\\cdot\\\overline\theta_n\\\overline\theta_1
 \end{array}\right)
=
{\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\theta_0\left(\begin{array}{cccccc}
1&1&1&1&\cdots&1\\
1&-1&1&1&\cdots&1\\
1&-1&-1&1&\cdots&1\\
\cdot&\cdot&\cdot&\cdot&&\cdot\\
\cdot&\cdot&\cdot&\cdot&&\cdot\\
1&-1&-1&-1&\cdots&-1
\end{array}\right)
\left(\begin{array}{c}
\alpha_1\\
\alpha_2\\
\cdot\\
\cdot\\
\cdot\\
\alpha_n
\end{array}
\right). \end{equation}
and the integral over ${\mathbb R}^n$ has indeed localised, to a set of $2^n$
regions of size of order one as $\theta_0\to\infty$, which become
infinitely separated in this limit.
nodes.statement_short: Decay of $\phi$ localises integrals to $2^n$ regions

nodes.name: Parity of region centres
nodes.statement:
The coordinates $\overline\theta_k$ of the
centres of these regions are either all even multiples
of $\theta_0/2$, or all odd multiples of $\theta_0/2$, depending on whether $n$
is even or odd.
nodes.statement_short: Centres are even or odd multiples of $\theta_0/2$

nodes.name: Measure factors in transition regions
nodes.statement:
For each region of integration we must consider the behaviours
of the `measure factors' $1/(1+e^{\epsilon(\theta_k)})$, $k=1\dots n$.
As for the function $L(\theta)$ discussed above, these factors exhibit
a series of plateaux interleaved by transition regions, at
$\theta\approx\theta_a\equiv (m{-}1{-}2a)\theta_0/2$, 
$a=1\dots m{-}2$. Within these
transition regions, the measure factors
are well-approximated in the $\theta_0\to\infty$ limit by the
functions $1/(1+e^{\epsilon_a})$, by (\ref{epsadef}).
nodes.statement_short: In transition regions measure factors become limiting pseudoenergies

nodes.name: Split into two categories
nodes.statement:
In between these
regions the measure factors are approximately constant, and can be
expressed in terms of the numbers $y_a|_{{\cal M}_m}=x_a|_{{\cal M}_{m-1}}$,
$a=1\dots m{-}1$. Taking these considerations into account,
the terms in the sum in (\ref{lng0}) fall into two categories:
nodes.statement_short: Elsewhere they are constants; terms split into two classes

nodes.name: Missing piece
nodes.statement:
A missing piece of the staircase discussion from the previous section
can now be filled in,
namely the formulae 
(\ref{lng0fodd}) and (\ref{lng0feven})
for the value of $\ln g^{\phantom o}_{0}|_{{\cal M}_m}$ when the bulk 
staircase theory is in
the vicinity of ${\cal M}_m$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the pending formula for $\ln g_0$

nodes.name: Reduce to UV limit
nodes.statement:
In terms of the limiting $g$-function
equations for ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_m$, this number is equal to the UV limit of
$\ln g^{\phantom o}_{A}(\hat{r}) + \ln g^{\phantom o}_{B}$ as $\hat{r}\to 0$.
nodes.statement_short: $\ln g_0$ on ${\cal M}_m$ is the UV limit of $\ln g_A+\ln g_B$

nodes.name: UV limit of $\ln g_A$
nodes.statement_short: UV limit of $\ln g_A$ is $\ln g_B$ at $m+1$; sum the closed forms

nodes.name: Start with UV
nodes.statement:
This can be checked directly.
Simplest is the UV limit.
nodes.statement_short: Check directly, starting with the UV limit

nodes.name: UV, $m$ odd
nodes.statement_short: Substitute plateau values for $m$ odd

nodes.name: UV, $m$ even
nodes.statement_short: Same for $m$ even

nodes.name: IR limit of $A$
nodes.statement_short: $A$ tends to a constant matrix $A_{\rm IR}$

nodes.name: Reduce to $B$ at $m-1$
nodes.statement:
To evaluate this sum, observe that the central $(m{-}4)\times(m{-}4)$
sub-matrix of $A_{\rm IR}$ is the matrix $B$ for ${\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}$.
Furthermore, the zero values of all entries in the first and final
rows means that the central $(m{-}4)\times(m{-}4)$ sub-matrix of 
$(A_{\rm IR})^n$ is just 
$(B|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}})^n$\,, 
and the entries on the first and final rows are again zero.
Hence the traces and antitraces of $(A_{\rm IR})^n$ are equal to those
of $(B|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}})^n$\,, and 
\begin{equation}
\ln g_{0_A}(\infty)|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m}}=\ln g_{0_B}|_{{\cal M} A^{(+)}_{m-1}}
\end{equation}

= -\mbox{Tr}\ln(I-M)
= -\ln\mbox{Det}(I-M) \end{equation}
